winner.title: Bigos
winner.source: NYT Cooking (Francis Lam, adapted from Monika Woods)

evidence.authenticity: Sauerkraut, fresh cabbage, beef, pork and kielbasa, caraway, allspice, bay, served with rye. Adapted from a Polish cook (Woods's mother's home version). Tomato and carrot are a legitimate home variant but not the classic prune, mushroom and juniper version. Intro explains the dish as the national dish and notes the scrap-meat tradition.
evidence.precision: 5 of 15 ingredients with weights; sizes given for cuts (1 1/2-inch, 1-inch, 1/4-inch slices). Sensory cues in steps: oil shimmers, golden brown, fragrant, onions soft, cabbage wilted and released juices. Explicit doneness at 2, 4 and 6 hours. Pot size vague (large, heavy pot).
evidence.testing: NYT test process, 305 ratings averaging 4.0. Explains the sear-then-deglaze-with-water method and how flavor and texture change with simmer time.
evidence.photos: Step photos are not in the schema (0). Page has many images but they could not be confirmed as process shots. Scored conservatively.
evidence.efficiency: Five steps, no wasted work. 3.5 to 7.5 hours stated and honest, since long simmering is the point. Searing in batches with a deglaze each time is slightly fussy.
evidence.access: All items are at a US grocery. Short-rib meat has a note; canned tomatoes and sauerkraut are easy.

winner.why: It beat the runner-up on precision and tested guidance (doneness described at 2, 4 and 6 hours), though the Serious Eats version is more traditional.

runnerUp.title: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
runnerUp.source: Serious Eats (Kate Williams, from A Polish Country House Kitchen by Anne Applebaum and Danielle Crittenden)

evidence.authenticity: Traditional multi-meat bigos with dried wild mushrooms, prunes, sauerkraut, fresh cabbage, red wine and kielbasa. Sourced from a Poland-based cookbook, with a description of the target texture.
evidence.precision: 8 of 15 ingredients with weights; 'small handful' of mushrooms is vague; cues such as sauerkraut very tender, meat falls apart, broth rich and brown. Pot size vague.
evidence.testing: Cookbook recipe republished with a description of the right consistency. No test-kitchen notes found.
evidence.photos: 0 step images in schema; photos not confirmed.
evidence.efficiency: Parallel prep of sauerkraut and cabbage while browning meat. 2.5 hours stated.
evidence.access: Venison is hard to find, and no substitute is given beyond a stewing cut. Dried wild mushrooms are fine.

runnerUp.why: More traditional, but less precise and with no test-kitchen backing.

candidates.disqualified: no structured data; not read further

notes: Scores for BBC, Polonist and Honest Food are rough estimates from read output. Polish-language sources were seen in search but not read. NYT also has a second version (Polish Hunter's Choucroute, 1018614) that was not read. Winner margin over Serious Eats is small; Serious Eats is the more traditional recipe if authenticity matters most.
